approach: Add `check_defined_terms(reading, request)` to crates/athena-core/src/reading.rs as one `step!` in `refusing_check`, right after `check_environment_reach` and before `check_boundary_and_repo_files`. Like its siblings `check_outcome_state` and `check_governance_coverage`, it returns Ok for a reading with no capability, a question, or no deliverable. It reduces the request to plain prose, finds the whole words ladder, rung, tier and layer (plural and possessive too), and refuses when a used term has no `Term <word>:` assumption. Plain prose excludes: generated root-cause lines (skipped by exact shape), quoted spans, parenthesised example lists and code-like tokens. The rule is also an eighth `READING_RULES` line in briefs.rs (outside the budgeted reader prompt). Revision: the quoted-mention accept case (criterion 2) is built from Athena's real generator, `athena_core::hestia::root_cause_request(&RepeatedCause, &Records)` (public, hestia.rs:453), called from the integration test with a RepeatedCause and two IntrospectionRecords whose class, cause and prevention text mention ladder, layer and tier. A self-check test pins the generator's line shapes, so a wording change in hestia.rs fails visibly. The hand-copied `root_cause_request(extra)` helper stays for the older cases and is not claimed to be the generator. The change also updates the cited-jobs replay (g6vy by `check_outcome_state`, 7bf8 by `check_defined_terms`, 0wtc by none), rewrites one `check_outcome_state` doc sentence, and adds a CHANGELOG entry and D164. Those declare `expected 3% of newly refused readings` as an estimate and name the false refusals. D164 asks the user to decide on narrowing tier and layer if the share recorded at verification is above 8%.

decisions.choice: Match structural words in plain request prose only: a `plain_request_prose` pre-pass, then the existing `request_words` tokenizer, then whole-word comparison (term, term+s, with a trailing `'s` stripped from the token first).
decisions.reason: `request_words` (reading.rs:3507) splits all text and ignores quoting, and its tokens keep `'` between letters, so "ladder's" would match nothing. The 7bf8 request quotes 'a ladder of requirements' and also uses the term in plain prose, so the pre-pass must drop the first and keep the second. Whole-word tokens keep stepladder, delayer, `ladder.md` and `layer_count` out.

rejected.option: Run `request_words` over the whole request
rejected.why: It ignores quoting, so generated root-cause requests (hestia.rs:466-489) that only quote the words would be refused.

rejected.option: Substring match
rejected.why: It refuses stepladder and delayer, which criterion 3 requires to pass.

rejected.option: Treat every parenthesised span as a non-use
rejected.why: It hides real uses such as '(the ladder, which ranks requirements)'.

decisions.choice: Skip generated lines by their exact shape. An `Introspection ` line is skipped only if it also holds ' (job ' and '); prevention it proposed:' (hestia.rs:486-488). `Failure class: `, `Cause: ` and `Fix the root cause of a repeated failure: ` lines are skipped only when the request also holds hestia's opening sentence 'The same cause has produced failures in more than one job.' (hestia.rs:467).
decisions.reason: The bare prefixes would drop a hand-written line such as 'Introspection of the ladder is needed.' or 'Cause: the ladder has no rung' whole. The anchor sentence and the full line shape tie the skip to text Athena generated. Unit cases pin that the hand-written forms are still uses.

rejected.option: Skip any line that starts with introspection, cause: or failure class:
rejected.why: Case-insensitive bare prefixes drop hand-written lines that use a term.

rejected.option: Do not skip generated lines and rely on quote stripping
rejected.why: The generated Cause and prevention text is free prose from earlier introspections, so it is not quoted.

rejected.option: Export the anchor sentence and line prefixes as pub consts in hestia.rs so both sides share them
rejected.why: hestia.rs is not a listed deliverable. A test that builds the case from the real generator and asserts its shapes gives the same protection without touching it.

decisions.choice: Quote and parenthesis handling: remove straight and curly double-quoted spans, backtick pairs, and single-quoted spans (opener after start/whitespace/`(` and before a letter or digit; closer after a non-space and before a non-alphanumeric; an unclosed opener stays as text). Scan per line. Remove a parenthesised span only if it has two or more commas or opens with e.g., i.e., such as, for example or like. Replace whitespace-delimited tokens containing `/`, `_` or `::` with a space.
decisions.reason: A single-comma parenthetical such as '(the ladder, which ranks requirements)' is a real use and stays counted. A list like '(ladder, layer, tier)' has two commas and is dropped. Per-line scanning means a stray apostrophe cannot swallow the rest of the request.

rejected.option: Drop any parenthesised span that holds a comma
rejected.why: It hides a real use with a single comma.

decisions.choice: A term is defined by an assumption that, trimmed and lowercased, starts `term <word>:` followed by at least 3 words. The word is normalised by dropping a trailing `s` or `'s` when the base form is in STRUCTURAL_TERMS, so `Term layers:` defines layer. The line may cite the defining file. No criterion naming the term is required.
decisions.reason: This copies the `Code survey:` convention (`code_surveys`, reading.rs:3832), which the reader already knows. It needs no new reading field.

rejected.option: Read docs/ontology.toml
rejected.why: Out of scope in the brief.

rejected.option: Also require a behavior criterion that names the term
rejected.why: A second condition for little gain. Criterion 1's accepted case carries one anyway.

rejected.option: Accept a definition in the reading summary
rejected.why: The summary has no fixed label, so a check on it would be lexical guessing.

decisions.choice: Skip conditions match the sibling checks: return Ok when `reading.capability.is_none()`, `reading.question.is_some()` or `reading.deliverables.is_empty()` (as `check_outcome_state` does at reading.rs:3681). The doc comment says so.
decisions.reason: Answers finding 3. Consistent gating means a reading that changes nothing is not asked for term definitions, and the doc comment states the condition instead of leaving it implied. `base_reading` in the corpus holds one deliverable (refusal_corpus.rs:162), so the corpus cases are checked.

rejected.option: Check readings with no deliverables too
rejected.why: It differs from both sibling checks and refuses readings that make no change; the doc would need a reason that does not exist.

decisions.choice: Place the step after `check_environment_reach` (reading.rs:3252) and before `check_boundary_and_repo_files`.
decisions.reason: Existing tests pin governance then outcome_state, and outcome_state then environment_reach. The new check reads only the reading and request, so it belongs before the file-comparing checks. `an_extra_check_with_no_case_is_reported` anchors on `check_reading_references`, which is unaffected.

rejected.option: Right after check_outcome_state
rejected.why: It breaks the environment_reach adjacency test.

rejected.option: Last
rejected.why: A missing file would be reported first, and the cheaper request-and-reading check would run last.

decisions.choice: Keep the four-word list (fixed by the brief) and state the false-refusal class as intended: priority tiers (plan.rs, drain.rs, config.rs, display.rs), a caching layer, and the repo's own ladder and rung are refused until a `Term` line restates them. Pin the class with corpus cases that expect a refusal. D164 asks the user to decide whether to narrow tier and layer if the share recorded at verification is above 8%.
decisions.reason: Answers finding 2. Narrowing the list is a user decision the brief has already made. Stating the limit in the doc comment and D164, pinning it with refusing cases, and handing the follow-up decision to the user makes any later narrowing a visible, deliberate change.

rejected.option: Drop 'tier' and 'layer' to cut false refusals
rejected.why: The brief fixes the list.

rejected.option: Leave the false-refusal class unstated
rejected.why: The refusal rate would be understated to the reader and the verifier.

decisions.choice: Build the criterion 2 accept case from the real generator. In refusal_corpus.rs add `generated_root_cause_request(sentence: Option<&str>)`, which builds a `RepeatedCause` (class `Some("Structural terms stay undefined (ladder, layer, tier)")`, a cause mentioning the ladder and the rung, two introspection ids, two job ids already used by the corpus, `request: None`) and a `Records` with two `IntrospectionRecord` values (prevention text such as 'Define the ladder, the layer and the tier before you read.'), then calls `athena_core::hestia::root_cause_request`. The optional sentence is spliced into the opening paragraph by `replace` on 'do not work around one instance.' so the bullets stay 3. The accept case splices in a sentence with a double-quoted word, a single-quoted word and a parenthesised list. The refusing companion splices in a plain use. A test `generated_request_has_the_generators_shapes` asserts the text holds the opening sentence, a `Failure class: ` line, a `Cause: ` line, `Introspection ` lines with ' (job ' and '); prevention it proposed:', and the title line.
decisions.reason: Answers finding 1. The old corpus helper `root_cause_request(extra)` (refusal_corpus.rs:236-254) is a hand copy with no opening sentence, no Failure class line and no Cause line, so it never exercises the anchor-gated skips. `hestia::root_cause_request` is public, its `RepeatedCause` fields and `store::Records` fields are public, and hestia's own tests call it (hestia.rs:2384, 3400, 3620). If hestia.rs rewords its lines, the shapes test and the accepted case fail, so the Risks claim is now true.

rejected.option: Keep using the hand-copied `root_cause_request(extra)` helper for the criterion 2 case
rejected.why: It does not hold the generator's lines and does not change when hestia.rs does.

rejected.option: A unit test in hestia.rs
rejected.why: hestia.rs is not a listed deliverable; the integration test reaches the same public function.

rejected.option: Build the text by hand-copying the generator's strings into the test
rejected.why: It is the same stale-copy fault the finding names.

decisions.choice: State the measurement path honestly. The doc comment, CHANGELOG and D164 declare 'expected 3% of newly refused readings' as an estimate. They say the measured share is recorded in the job's replay record at verification (`replay_stage` then `run.record`), where the verifier sees it, and is shown to the producer only in a held send-back (`replay_problem`). The producer writes a measured figure only if a send-back reports one. No test asserts a measured figure.
decisions.reason: run/producer.rs:370-399 passes the replay to the producer only as a held problem. The producer snapshot has no records/, so it cannot run the replay. A needle for a measured share could never be satisfied reliably.

rejected.option: Producer reads the loop-replay line and writes the measured value
rejected.why: The line goes to Athena's UI, which the producer cannot read.

rejected.option: A test needle for 'measured share where it differs'
rejected.why: The producer cannot know whether the share differs, so the needle is unsatisfiable.

decisions.choice: Add an eighth line to `READING_RULES` in briefs.rs, at most 220 characters, and raise the size bound in its test to just above the printed length.
decisions.reason: The brief rule list is outside the budgeted reader prompt set (CONTRACT, READER_FRAME, defaults, catalog), so no prompt budget changes. The reader learns the rule before its first read.

rejected.option: Rely on the refusal text only
rejected.why: It costs a refused first read, and the brief asks for the READING_RULES test to be updated.

rejected.option: Edit the reader prompt
rejected.why: It has 3 tokens of room, and prompt changes are out of scope.

decisions.choice: Update `delivery_verb_replay_over_the_cited_jobs` in place and add `defined_terms_replay_over_the_cited_jobs`. Leave D161 and the old CHANGELOG entry untouched.
decisions.reason: The old test asserts that the 7bf8 outcome is `None` (refusal_corpus.rs:516-518), which the new check makes false. D161 is append-only. The old CHANGELOG wording ('covers 1 of the 3 cited jobs' for check_outcome_state) is asserted at refusal_corpus.rs:527 and stays true for that check.

rejected.option: Edit D161
rejected.why: The decision log is append-only; the mirror rule rejects it.

rejected.option: Delete the old replay test
rejected.why: It is the measured proof for check_outcome_state.

decisions.choice: Rest criterion 4 on gate-level tests. Add a reading.rs test helper `refuser_for(reading, request)` (the existing `gate_refuser` fixes the request, reading.rs:10279-10281) and assert `refuser_for(..) == Some("check_defined_terms")`. The corpus refusing case checks the same name.
decisions.reason: Without the `step!` line, `refusing_check` returns None for the undefined-ladder reading, so the gate tests fail. A test that filters a string copy of the source tests only the extractor.

rejected.option: Source-doctoring test on READING_SOURCE
rejected.why: It tests the extractor and not the gate.

(a) Skip an `Introspection ` line only if it also holds ' (job ' and '); prevention it proposed:'. If the request contains 'The same cause has produced failures in more than one job.', also skip lines that start (case-sensitive) with `Failure class: `, `Cause: ` or `Fix the root cause of a repeated failure: `. (b) Per line, remove straight and curly double-quoted spans, backtick pairs, and single or curly single-quoted spans (opener after start, whitespace or `(` and before a letter or digit; closer after a non-space and before a non-alphanumeric; an unclosed opener stays as text). (c) Remove parenthesised spans that hold two or more commas or begin with `e.g.`, `i.e.`, `such as`, `for example` or `like`. (d) Replace whitespace-delimited tokens containing `/`, `_` or `::` with a space. Add `defined_terms(reading) -> BTreeSet<String>`: trimmed assumptions that lowercase-start with `term <word>:` and have at least 3 words after the colon; normalise the word by dropping a trailing `s` or `'s` when the base form is in STRUCTURAL_TERMS. Add `pub fn check_defined_terms(reading, request) -> Result<()>`: return Ok when `capability` is None, `question` is Some or `deliverables` is empty (as `check_outcome_state` does). Tokenise `plain_request_prose` with `request_words`, strip a trailing `'s`, find tokens equal to a term or term+`s` in order of first use, and bail when any is undefined with one line: 'the reading was refused because the request uses {terms} as a structural term but the reading does not define {it/them}; ...add an assumption that starts `Term ladder:` (one per term) saying what it means in this job, and cite the file that defines it if there is one'.

It names the root cause ('readings are not checked against the outcome the user observes, so structural terms stay undefined'), cites 20261014-174815-7bf8 and 20261017-173508-0wtc, says the check skips a reading with no capability, a question, or no deliverable, like the governance and outcome-state checks, and says 'This check refuses more readings; the higher refusal rate is intended.' It says that repo-defined terms (ladder, rung) are refused until restated with a `Term ladder:` line that may cite the defining file, and that plain technical uses of tier (priority tiers) and layer (a caching layer) are refused too. It lists what is not covered: quoted mentions, terms outside the list, and the Hermes term of 0wtc. Add `step!(check_defined_terms(reading, request));` after `step!(check_environment_reach(reading));` in `refusing_check`, and add `[`check_defined_terms`]` to the doc order of `check_reading_acceptance`. Rewrite the check_outcome_state sentence at reading.rs:3659-3660: 7bf8 is caught by [`check_defined_terms`], 0wtc by no check. risks.risk: The 3% figure is an estimate. The planner cannot see records/, the producer cannot run the loop replay, and the real share of past requests that use these words in plain prose is unknown. Tier and layer are common words.
risks.mitigation: The text labels 3% an estimate and says the measured share is recorded in the replay record at verification, where the verifier sees it. The producer writes a measured figure only if a held send-back (`replay_problem`) reports one. Over 8%, the producer narrows false refusals (for example the code-token skip) and reports the rest, and D164 hands the tier and layer narrowing decision to the user.

risks.risk: Quote handling over-strips (a stray apostrophe swallows a use) or under-strips (a quoted mention is counted).
risks.mitigation: Scan per line and leave an unclosed opener as text. Unit tests cover apostrophes in "Sri's" and "don't", an unclosed quote, curly quotes, backticks, possessive "ladder's" (counted as a use), and a plain use beside quotes (companion corpus case, refused).

risks.risk: The generated-line skip drops a hand-written line, or fails to skip a generated one.
risks.mitigation: Skip by exact shape: an Introspection line needs ' (job ' and '); prevention it proposed:'; Cause:, Failure class: and the title need hestia's opening sentence. The accepted corpus case is built from the real `hestia::root_cause_request`, and `generated_request_has_the_generators_shapes` asserts the shapes, so a rewording in hestia.rs fails a test. Unit cases pin the hand-written forms in both directions.

risks.risk: The test builds an `IntrospectionRecord` by hand (about 24 fields), which breaks if the record type gains a field.
risks.mitigation: A compile error in the test names the field, and hestia's own test helper (hestia.rs:2836-2868) must change at the same time, so the repair is a copy of that update. The helper is one function in the corpus file.

risks.risk: A parenthesised list with a single comma, such as '(ladder, layer)', is counted as a use, and a long parenthetical with two commas that holds a real use is dropped.
risks.mitigation: The rule (two or more commas, or an example opener) is stated in the doc comment and covered by unit cases for each shape. The residual error is a false refusal, which the reader repairs with a Term line, rather than a silent acceptance of a main use.

risks.risk: The rules section in briefs.rs exceeds the 2600-byte bound with an eighth line (about 2570 bytes is an estimate, not a measurement).
risks.mitigation: Run `cargo test -p athena-context`. The failure prints the actual section length, and the producer sets the bound just above it. The new line stays at or under 220 characters.

risks.risk: The old cited-jobs replay asserts the 7bf8 request is accepted, which now fails, and the old CHANGELOG/D161 wording could be broken.
risks.mitigation: Edit the replay test in step 5. Leave D161 and the old CHANGELOG line unchanged, so the existing 'covers 1 of the 3 cited jobs' assertions still hold for check_outcome_state.

risks.risk: 0wtc could be wrongly claimed as caught or not caught, because the real recorded request may differ from the text in CITED_REQUESTS.
risks.mitigation: The 0wtc assertion is `outcome.is_none()` on the text at refusal_corpus.rs:467-472, plus a scan that the text holds none of the four words. The doc comment and D164 state that the Hermes term is not covered.

risks.risk: A new corpus case is refused first by an earlier check (an unknown path, a bullet count mismatch), so it fails for the wrong reason.
risks.mitigation: The producer runs the `refusal_corpus` target, which prints each mismatch with the case id. The generated request has 3 acceptance bullets (hestia.rs:3620-3625); the 7bf8-shaped cases copy the existing 7bf8 case shape. The Files line `crates/` in the generated text is checked by running the case; if an earlier check refuses it, the producer sets `repo_files()` or `referenced` as the existing root-cause case does.

demonstrations.method: Run the real gate `refusing_check` on two corpus cases built from the recorded 7bf8 request (shared const `REQUEST_7BF8`, extracted from `CITED_REQUESTS`, refusal_corpus.rs:456). Case A, `structural-term-ladder-undefined-in-7bf8-request`, uses `base_reading` (one deliverable) with no Term line and expects a refusal by check_defined_terms. Case B, `structural-term-ladder-defined-and-named-by-a-behavior-criterion-accepted`, adds an assumption `Term ladder: ...` that cites docs/guide.md (in `repo_files()`) and a behavior criterion naming the ladder via `with_behavior`; it expects acceptance. A reading.rs unit test also checks that `Term ladders: ...` defines ladder.
demonstrations.observes: Case A gives Some(("check_defined_terms", err)); the error starts 'the reading was refused because', names ladder and shows the `Term ladder:` repair. Case B gives None. `corpus_cases_get_the_expected_outcome` and `the_wrapper_agrees_with_refusing_check_on_every_case` pass. I read the test names and case structure and ran nothing.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without `check_defined_terms` and its step line, Case A is accepted and `corpus_cases_get_the_expected_outcome` fails. If the check ignored the Term line, Case B is refused.

demonstrations.method: Run the real gate on a request built by Athena's real generator. `generated_root_cause_request(Some(sentence))` in refusal_corpus.rs calls `athena_core::hestia::root_cause_request` (public, hestia.rs:453) with a `RepeatedCause` and a `Records` holding two `IntrospectionRecord` values. The class, cause and prevention text mention ladder, layer and tier, so the real `Failure class:`, `Cause:`, title and `Introspection <id> (job <job>); prevention it proposed:` lines carry the words. The spliced sentence adds a double-quoted word, a single-quoted word and a parenthesised list '(ladder, layer, tier)'. The case `structural-term-quoted-or-cited-mentions-are-accepted` uses `base_reading` with no Term lines, `referenced` set as in `root-cause-cites-two-jobs-without-relying`, and 3 bullets. Source: 'job 20261107-110049-k8c2 style; text built by hestia::root_cause_request from a constructed RepeatedCause; not the recorded request (records/ is absent)'. Companions: `structural-term-plain-use-beside-quoted-mentions-is-refused` (the same generator text with 'Use the ladder to decide what to change.' spliced in; refused), `structural-term-possessive-use-is-refused` ('the ladder's rungs'; refused), and a case on the old hand-copied helper with an Introspection line only (accepted, shape skip without the anchor). The test `generated_request_has_the_generators_shapes` asserts the generated text holds the opening sentence, a `Failure class: ` line, a `Cause: ` line, the Introspection shape and the title line. Unit tests in reading.rs call `check_defined_terms` on each quoting shape and pin that a hand-written 'Introspection of the ladder is needed.' and an anchorless 'Cause: the ladder is undefined' are still uses. Tags `structural-term-plain-prose`, `structural-term-quoted-or-cited` and `structural-term-defined` are added to INPUT_FORMS (34 becomes 37).
demonstrations.observes: The generated quoted-only request gives None from `refusing_check` with a reading that has no Term lines. The companion cases give Some("check_defined_terms"). The shapes test passes, so the accepted case really goes through the anchor-gated skips. `corpus_covers_the_listed_input_forms` passes because each new tag has a case. I read the helper and the generator and ran nothing.
demonstrations.fails_without: If quoted or generated mentions counted as uses, the accepted case is refused. If the generated-line skip were removed, the accepted case and `defined_terms_ignores_generated_lines_quotes_and_parentheses` fail. If the skip were blanket, the plain-use companion would be accepted and fail. If the bare-prefix skip came back, the hand-written Introspection and Cause unit cases fail. If hestia.rs reworded its lines, the shapes test fails.

open_questions: User: If the replay at verification records more than 8% of newly refused readings (the declared 3% plus the 5-point margin), should the list drop 'layer' or 'tier', or should the declared share rise through a revised reading? The planner cannot see records/, and the producer can neither run the replay nor edit the accepted reading's declared figure. D164 records this as the user's decision.

User: Should hand-written requests that use 'tier' (Athena's priority tiers) or 'layer' (a caching layer) in a plain technical sense, and requests about the repo's own ladder and rung, stay refused until the reading restates them with a Term line? This plan says yes and pins it with corpus cases, as the brief fixes the list.
